transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-04-08 09:30 UTC
Duration: 38 min
Attendees: Sarah Mitchell (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Indigo Sails - Head of ML), Marcus Lowe (Indigo Sails - Infra), Ana Ruiz (Product)

[00:00] Sarah (AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, um let's do quick intros then we'll jump into what you're trying to build.
[00:18] Priya: Hi all, I'm Priya. We're building an in-app search and assistance layer for Indigo Sails customers, want low latency for interactive results.
[00:28] Marcus: Marcus here, I'll be the infra contact. We care about egress control and residency.
[00:34] Ana: Ana, product, mainly around rollout timing and pricing.
[00:42] Sarah: Great. Diego, do you want to kick off on latency/cost tradeoffs?
[00:47] Diego (SE): Sure. So typical paths: self-serve hosted API is fastest to first token, free credits to prototype. Dedicated/reserved gives predictable throughput and can be in a VPC for more isolation. There's also Private on-prem option if you need air-gapped.
[01:06] Priya: When you say "fastest to first token" like how fast? Our target p95 is around 300-400ms for short queries.
[01:14] Diego: For short context, on hosted with optimized models we often see 80-220ms p50, p95 in the 200-500ms range depending on model and sequence length. Dedicated with reserved GPUs lowers jitter and can push p95 closer to your 300ms goal for small prompts if you tune batching.
[01:36] Marcus: Hmm ok. What about cost—we're doing a cost model comparing Anthropic and OpenAI and your dedicated pricing.
[01:44] Sarah: We'll send a hosted vs dedicated SKU sheet. The hosted pay-as-you-go is useful for prototype, we give credits that take you to first calls. Dedicated is monthly commit but unit cost is lower at scale.
[01:58] Priya: Do you offer private KMS or HSM integrations? Our security lead wants customer-managed keys.
[02:05] Diego: Yes, Redwood Private supports KMS integrations, we can integrate customer keys via AWS KMS or bring-your-own HSM depending on deployment. For hosted we have envelope encryption and can discuss bring-your-own-key for enterprise tiers.
[02:21] Marcus: Network wise, how would VPC peering work? We have strict egress rules.
[02:27] Diego: For Dedicated/Private we support VPC peering and private connectivity. For hosted we'd do controlled egress and dedicated private connectivity on premium plans; otherwise it's public API with IP allow lists and SSO.
[02:44] Ana: Any compliance docs? SOC2? ISO?
[02:48] Sarah: We have SOC2 and ISO 27001 for enterprise; I'll share the SOC2 report and the security FAQ link after the call.
[02:58] Priya: That'll help, thanks.
[03:03] Diego: Quick note on cache and batching—if your UI does short prefix queries we can suggest KV caching and small batch sizes to hit latency SLOs while lowering token cost. Some customers saw 20-40% token cost reduction with prefix caching.
[03:20] Priya: Could you explain KV cache? Is that the key-value cache in the model runtime?
[03:25] Diego: Yeah it's the KV cache for the attention keys/values, pardon I said KV "cash" earlier, sorry. The platform caches prefix computations so repeated or incremental typing doesn't recompute everything.
[03:36] Marcus: Nice. For the benchmark, what do you need from us?
[03:40] Diego: A list of representative prompts, average and max context lengths, concurrency targets, and auth headers. We'll run a short throughput and latency run on hosted and then propose a dedicated baseline.
[03:54] Sarah: We'll also include an example script and approximate cost for a 1k-request benchmark.
[04:00] Priya: Timeline—if we like results we're targeting a pilot next week or the week after.
[04:06] Sarah: Sounds doable. We'll aim to get the benchmark spec in two business days.
[04:12] [silence 00:20]
[04:33] Marcus: Real world question — our docs say data retention policies, do you store prompts or persist logs?
[04:40] Diego: Hosted stores ephemeral logs for telemetry unless you opt out; enterprise hosted/dedicated can be configured for no retention and audit trails sent to your logging endpoints. Private on-prem gives you full control.
[04:55] Priya: Good, we need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[04:59] Diego: Yep we can ship logs, and we have token-level cost breakdowns in the console to help debugging.
[05:10] Sarah: Any blockers on your side for starting with hosted credits?
[05:15] Ana: We're mostly worried about compliance and the demo looking like production latency. If hosted is too variable we might go dedicated.
[05:23] Diego: For demos you can use dedicated short-term or use priority routing and smaller batch sizes to reduce variance on hosted. But yes dedicated reduces tail latency.
[05:36] Priya: We heard about model fallbacks — if you run out of capacity do you automatically fallback to other variants?
[05:43] Diego: We have smart routing with fallback policies. If a region or a specific GPU pool is constrained we can route to a compatible quantized variant. We'll surface quality differences in the console so you can set policy.
[05:58] Marcus: Does private deployment support our on-prem GPU racks?
[06:03] Diego: There's an on-prem package; needs an infra vetting. You'd run the control plane privately and the runtime in your cluster. It is more involved but supported for regulated workloads.
[06:18] [short chuckle]
[06:22] Priya: For the pilot, we want to try hosted first to validate UX then move to dedicated. Would that path make sense?
[06:29] Sarah: That's our most common path — prototyping on hosted credits then scale to dedicated when traffic stabilizes and SLA needed.
[06:35] Ana: Ok timeline question — how long to stand up dedicated if we decide?
[06:39] Diego: If you commit we can provision pools in 2-4 weeks depending on capacity. Private could be longer due to networking.
[06:47] Priya: Are there any limitations on model catalog on dedicated? We need some newer open models and quantized variants.
[06:54] Diego: We support a curated catalog. Most open models are available; dedicated supports custom variants and quantization profiles. If you need a specific model we can add to the catalog as part of onboarding.
[07:10] Marcus: We are sensitive to egress costs — any data residency options for EU customers?
[07:16] Sarah: Yes regions matter. For hosted we can route traffic to EU regions; Dedicated/Private can be deployed in-region for residency. We'll capture your region preference in the pilot spec.
[07:30] Priya: Ok, what do we need to accept the free credits and sign up?
[07:34] Sarah: Self-serve sign up takes a couple minutes. We'll provision trial credits for the account and you can start calling the API right away. I can send a step-by-step quickstart doc.
[07:45] Ana: Please send the quickstart doc. Our PM will run the first token test.
[07:51] Sarah: Will do.
[07:55] Diego: One more infra note — for VPC peering we need a minimal firewall egress list and CIDR ranges; Marcus can share offline.
[08:05] Marcus: I'll compile and share that with you.
[08:08] [brief pause]
[08:12] Priya: Any known regressions with model updates? We need quality monitoring.
[08:18] Diego: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to evals and prompt sets. You can pin model versions to avoid unexpected behavior.
[08:29] Priya: Perfect.
[08:32] Ana: Ok other questions — what's support like during pilot?
[08:36] Sarah: We'll assign a CSM for pilots over a certain commit level, and SE support for the benchmark run. For quickstarts we handle Slack/email during business hours.
[08:49] [longer silence 00:15]
[09:05] Diego: Quick note about tokenization — if you have long documents we recommend embeddings + rerank to reduce token usage and cost.
[09:14] Priya: We'll send sample docs for that too.
[09:18] Sarah: Great. Let's recap next steps.
[09:21] Sarah: Action items — I'll share pricing sheet, quickstart link and SOC2. Diego will draft benchmark spec. Marcus will share firewall/CIDR. Priya will confirm compliance owners.
[09:34] Ana: Sounds good, we'll aim to spin up the quickstart this week.
[09:38] Sarah: Thanks all. We'll follow up via email with links and set the pilot kickoff in calendar.
[09:43] Priya: Thanks everyone. Bye.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions (KV cache heard as "K-V cash"), speaker overlaps, and filler words preserved.
